text: Proposition forty-four sets a spending rule for private
nonprofit safety-net clinics.
These clinics serve many low-income and uninsured patients.
Covered clinics would have to spend at least
ninety percent
of annual revenue on health care services,
leaving no more than ten percent for other
expenses.
A clinic falling short would owe a penalty
equal to the shortfall.
It could recover that money by complying within
five years.
Temporary waivers would be available in some circumstances.
A voter might want a larger share of
clinic revenue devoted to services for patients, with
reporting and consequences for falling short.
Another voter could worry that a rigid limit
constrains necessary support costs,
adds fees, or makes some clinics financially fragile.
Yes adopts the new spending rule;
no leaves existing reporting and spending requirements in
place.
